post.description:
Queue a font conversion for a file already in object storage.

Emits a ``Server-Timing`` header (total wall time) for client-side
observability.

Flow:
  1. Client calls ``/upload/`` (or presigns directly), gets ``s3_key``.
  2. Client calls this endpoint with ``s3_key`` + ``target_format``.
  3. Backend records the job, dispatches to ``celery-docs`` worker.
  4. Worker downloads, converts, uploads result, updates row.
  5. Client polls ``/conversion/{id}/`` then ``/{id}/download/``.

get.summary: Get structured pricing plans for frontend display. PP 2.1
get.description:
Returns the active pricing plans in a structured format optimized for frontend display.

**Unit:** 1,000 credits = $1 · 1 query = 7 credits.

**Features included in all plans:**
- Access to all features
- Email support
- Cancel anytime
- No refund policy

**Plan Details:**
- **Free**: 1,000 credits/month (~33/day), recharged daily
- **Pro Monthly**: $9.99/month for 10,000 credits (auto-renewing)
- **Pro Annual**: $99.99/year for 10,000 credits/month (~17% savings)
- **Premium**: $19.99/month for 22,000 credits (auto-renewing)
- **Pay-as-you-go**: $1 per 1,000 credits, pay only for what you use

Each plan carries `provider_ids` (Stripe price + Apple/Google product IDs) for hybrid checkout.

**Public endpoint** - No authentication required. Perfect for pricing pages and marketing.

Use Cases

This endpoint is typically used for:

    ✅ Users viewing their own purchase history

    ✅ Admins monitoring all purchase transactions

    ✅ Building purchase history dashboards

    ✅ Tracking payment statuses and amounts

    ✅ Auditing billing transactions

get.summary: Stripe checkout return callback. Backend verifies payment then redirects to frontend.
get.description:
Stripe Checkout redirect target.

Stripe sends the user here after payment (success or cancel). We:
- Fetch the Checkout Session from Stripe using the secret key
- Reuse the common completion logic (same as webhook) to finalize purchase
- Redirect browser to the original next_url (if provided) or fallback frontend page

LoginRequest.description:
Request model for user login. Supports traditional username/password/email, Google OAuth, and Apple Sign-In authentication.

For Google OAuth authentication:
- Tokens can be provided in request body (legacy method)
- Tokens can be read from HTTPOnly cookies (recommended - set automatically after OAuth callback)
- If tokens are in cookies, no need to include them in request body

For Apple Sign-In authentication:
- Tokens can be provided in request body (legacy method)
- Tokens can be read from HTTPOnly cookies (recommended - set automatically after OAuth callback)
- If tokens are in cookies, no need to include them in request body
